Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups we promised to confirm: 

- Data residency: Acme asked for US-only storage for inference request/response payloads and logs.
- Region pinning: ability to pin traffic for specific customers/routes to a single geographic region (US).
- Cross-region failover: what happens if US region has an outage — can failover be limited to other US zones only?
- Backups and DR: are backups replicated cross-region or can they be restricted to US? Recovery RTO/RPO expectations.
- Logging & retention: default retention windows, ability to disable request/response retention, and access to audit logs.
- PII handling: options for redaction/masking, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys.

Action items I promised to follow up on:
1) Confirm region pinning semantics (route-level vs tenant-level) and whether failover can be constrained to US-only.
2) Provide clear backup/DR options (managed snapshots vs customer S3, replication behavior).
3) Confirm default logging retention and how to opt-out for PII-sensitive payloads.
4) Share SOC2 / security docs and a short design note on region pinning.

Marissa / Vanessa — tagging you for the technical answers (items 1–3) and attachment of our region-pinning design doc.

Samantha / Tom — we'll aim to get you answers by EOD and propose a short technical workshop next week to walk through options. Does Thursday 3/28 11:00 PT work for you?

Thanks Aditya —
Appreciate the recap. A few clarifying Qs from the security team so we can triage internally before the workshop: 

1) Region pinning: is this configurable per-route (we have some products that must remain in US while others can be multi-region) or only per-tenant? Can we enforce region pinning at the API key level?

2) Cross-region failover: if the primary US region becomes unavailable, will Redwood spin up/elect a replica in EU/APAC by default or is failover restricted to other US availability zones? We need guarantee that no customer data is automatically replicated outside the US without prior approval.

3) Backups: where are backups stored? Are managed snapshots encrypted and stored in Redwood-managed buckets (and if so, are they replicated cross-region)? Alternatively, can we configure Redwood to write encrypted backups to our own S3 bucket in US-only regions?

4) Logs & retention: what is default retention for request/response payloads and audit logs? Do you offer an option to disable retention of request/response data entirely?

5) KMS/customer keys: can we provide our own KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) for both runtime encryption and backups?

Security is flagging item 2 and 3 as blockers for procurement until we have concrete options. I've attached our security questionnaire (acme-security-questionnaire.pdf).

Thanks — happy to take the workshop if 3/28 11:00 PT works.

Aditya — answers below (short/consumer-friendly bullets). Attaching the design doc we discussed.

1) Region pinning:
- Supported at both tenant and route level. You can pin by customer tenant, API key, or route. Route-level pinning is commonly used when customers have mixed-product needs.
- Implementation: traffic routing policy attaches to a deployment cluster in the specified region. No data leaves the pinned region during normal operation.

2) Cross-region failover:
- Failover behavior is configurable per-tenant. Default behavior is to fail over to a pre-warmed pool in the same region (different AZs) to avoid cross-region replication.
- If you opt into cross-region failover, we will only do so with explicit agreement and we can gate that with a signed change request. There is no automatic replication to EU/APAC without customer approval.

3) Backups & DR:
- Two options: (A) Redwood-managed encrypted snapshots stored in our US-only storage (no cross-region replication by default), or (B) Customer-managed backups: Redwood can write encrypted snapshots directly to a customer S3 bucket (us-east-1 or us-west-2) controlled by the customer.
- Snapshots are encrypted with KMS; we support BYOK (customer-managed KMS) for both runtime and snapshot encryption.
- RTO/RPO: typical managed snapshot restore is ~2–4 hours depending on dataset size; we can provide dedicated DR runbooks and expedited restores under enterprise SLA.

4) Logs & retention:
- Default: request/response payloads retained 30 days, audit logs retained 365 days.
- You can opt out of storing request/response payloads entirely for a tenant; in that case we keep only metadata and audit logs.
- We also offer automatic PII redaction pipelines and field-level masking for supported payload formats.

5) KMS / keys:
- BYOK supported for runtime and backups; keys can be restricted to a US region.

Docs & links: https://docs.redwood.com/deployments/region-pinning, https://docs.redwood.com/security/byok

Attachment: redwood-region-pinning-design.pdf
